name: Moving-magnet induction test
summary: Faraday showed that pushing a magnet into a coil, or pulling it out, makes a brief electric current, while a magnet held still makes none.
description: A cylindrical permanent magnet is inserted into and withdrawn from a hollow coil connected to a galvanometer; motion gives opposite current impulses, and a stationary magnet gives none.
